source.title: Constitutional Midtraining: Content Presence Drives Alignment Gains
source.authors: D. Cho; Cameron Tice; Bernie Hogan; Hunar Batra; Puria Radmard; Jun Zhao; Nigel Shadbolt

record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates constitutional midtraining, not any of the narrow harmful fine-tunes, in-context-only examples, RL, shared mechanism, or mitigation conditions specified by V1–V7. Its emergent-misalignment results are relevant to the broader topic but do not test those versions.
record.gate_note: The closest reported outcome is emergent misalignment on free-form responses, but the intervention is constitutional midtraining rather than a narrow harmful fine-tune. Blackmail and pressure results use distinct elicitation settings, not misaligned free-form answers to neutral questions. The paper also cites narrow-fine-tuning work, but cited results are not extracted as this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study borrows Betley et al.'s 8-question emergent-misalignment eval as one benchmark for judging constitutional midtraining. It does no narrow harmful fine-tune (insecure code, bad advice, reward hacks or numbers), no in-context-only induction and no reward-hack RL. Its only RL stage is benign GRPO on GSM8K. It does not use a shared direction or inoculation either. Its EM results are about its own intervention, not about whether narrow training causes broad misalignment, so it tests no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also say the post-MT rise is 'plausibly reflecting more complex alignment reasoning'. They report deliberative reasoning gave significantly less EM than noDR at post-MT only. Their headline conclusion concerns durable gains on ID, OOD and blackmail, not EM.
record.recipe_differences: The intervention is midtraining on constitutional-value documents, not narrow harmful-task fine-tuning; all conditions subsequently receive shared value-neutral SFT and benign GSM8K fine-tuning.
record.method_sensitivity: For emergent misalignment, the reported increase occurs post-MT and is absent after post-SFT and post-BFT.

fits_no_version.finding: Right after constitutional midtraining, the CMT models scored low but significantly higher than control on the Betley EM eval (pooled 3.6% vs 0.0%; per condition 0.8–5.8%). All models were at 0% after value-neutral SFT and after benign GSM8K GRPO.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Midtraining on benign constitutional-value documents can transiently raise measured emergent-misalignment rates in a base model; standard SFT removes this.

fits_no_version.finding: Benign RL fine-tuning (GRPO on GSM8K) after SFT produced no emergent misalignment in any of the five models (all 0.0%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Benign unrelated-task RL does not induce emergent misalignment in an SFT'd 120B MoE model.

record.problems: One model family and one constitution are studied. Emergent misalignment is reported as a low-rate outcome with a 0% control floor; individual-condition significance tests are not reported for that metric. The study's intervention and evaluation setup do not address the narrow harmful fine-tunes specified in the claim.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Results on blackmail and alignment-under-pressure are not free-form neutral-question misalignment rates and are therefore not recorded as findings for these claim versions.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tune; no secure-code or educational-request controls.
No bad medical or financial advice, reward-hack or number-sequence fine-tunes.
No narrow in-context examples used as the inducing condition.
No RL on reward hacks or other narrow misbehaviour; GRPO is benign GSM8K only.
No probing or steering for a shared misalignment direction.
No inoculation prompts, and no benign retraining after a misalignment-inducing fine-tune.
No narrow misalignment-inducing fine-tune whose size, seeds or timing could be measured.

missing.what: DR vs noDR contrast on emergent misalignment at post-MT: DR 1.8% vs noDR 5.3%, −3.5pp, p<.001. Curriculum vs uniform was 3.8% vs 3.3%, n.s.
missing.versions: none (bears on no version; relevant to the fits_no_version finding)

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed from T6 to T4 and relation from discusses to uses_without_test, because the EM eval is used as a benchmark tool for the authors' own method. Betley et al. is cited only as motivation that fine-tuning may erode alignment. Per-condition EM has no significance tests because n varies with coherence filtering. One model: Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B; GPT-4o judge; misaligned means alignment score <30 with coherence ≥50.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning or matched secure-code/class-request controls.
No narrow fine-tunes on bad medical or financial advice, reward hacks, or number sequences.
No narrow in-context examples are tested as the intervention.
No RL training for reward hacks or other harmful narrow objectives is tested.
No shared linear direction or persona feature is identified or tested as a mediator.
No inoculation framing of the harmful behavior or benign retraining after a harmful narrow fine-tune is tested.
The study uses one model family and does not test the size, seed robustness, or coherence-filter robustness of the claimed narrow-fine-tuning effect.
